"""Batched quantum LNS on Qoro's cloud: large rounding windows, one per day, run in parallel.

Days interact only with their neighbours (rebalancing), so rounding windows on days of the
same parity (0, 2, 4, ... or 1, 3, 5, ...) are independent: their exact energy changes add
up.  Each round builds one window per day of one parity, sends every QAOA program to the
Qoro cloud at once (threads; each program = 2 circuits at transferred angles), and applies
every improving window together.  Same QUBOs and QAOA family as qlns.py (Dicke + ring XY,
p layers, angles transferred from the local runs), only wider.

    python portfolio_quantum/cloud_batch.py --inst po_a400_t15_orig --lam 1e-3 --start best \
        --kround 24 --rounds 8
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

import qlns
import qaoa_solver as qs

qc, ps = qlns.qc, qlns.ps


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--inst", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--lam", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--start", default="best")
    ap.add_argument("--kround", type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--shots", type=int, default=4000)
    ap.add_argument("--noise", type=float, default=0.1)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--angles", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "angles" / "a050_l1e-3.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--local", action="store_true", help="Maestro simulator instead of the cloud (testing)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    p = ps.Problem(a.inst, a.lam)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(a.seed)
    if a.start == "best":
        v0 = qc.load_v(p, qc.best_known_file(p.stem))
    elif a.start == "empty":
        v0 = np.zeros((p.T, p.n), dtype=np.int64)
    else:
        v0 = qc.load_v(p, Path(a.start))
    s = qc.State(p, v0)
    start = s.obj
    svc = None
    if not a.local:
        from divi.backends import QoroService
        svc = QoroService()
        credits0 = float(svc.get_credit_balance()["balance"])
    # one solver per thread (programs keep their own state); angles read-only (no retraining)
    solvers = [qs.QAOASolver(layers=a.layers, shots=a.shots, cloud=not a.local, seed=a.seed + k,
                             retrain_every=10**9, angles_file=None) for k in range(p.T)]
    lib = json.loads(Path(a.angles).read_text())
    for sv in solvers:
        sv.library["xy"] = np.array(lib[f"xy_p{a.layers}"])
        if lib.get(f"x_p{a.layers}"):
            sv.library["x"] = np.array(lib[f"x_p{a.layers}"])
    print(f"{p.stem}: start {start}, {p.qubo_vars} QUBO variables, cloud={not a.local}", flush=True)
    log = []
    for r in range(a.rounds):
        parity = r % 2
        days = [t for t in range(p.T - 1) if t % 2 == parity]
        windows = []
        for t in days:
            w = qlns.round_window(s, t, rng, a.kround, noise=a.noise * rng.random())
            if w is not None:
                windows.append((t, w))
        t0 = time.time()

        def job(item):
            k, (t, (tmp, moves, hw)) = item
            if hw is None and len(moves) > 22:  # free-weight windows would add slack: keep them small
                moves = moves[:22]
            res = qlns.run_window(s, tmp, moves, solvers[k], True, hw=hw)
            return t, moves, res

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(windows)) as ex:
            results = list(ex.map(job, enumerate(windows)))
        v_new = s.v.copy()
        gains = []
        for t, moves, res in results:
            if res is None:
                continue
            v2, obj, ncand, e = res
            if obj < s.obj:  # this day's window alone improves the incumbent
                v_new[t] = v2[t]
                gains.append((t, obj - s.obj, len(moves)))
        new_obj = p.objective(v_new)
        expect = s.obj + sum(g for _, g, _ in gains)
        assert new_obj == expect, (new_obj, expect)  # independence of same-parity days
        qubits = max(len(m) for _, m, _ in results)
        print(f"round {r} parity {parity}: {len(windows)} programs (<= {qubits} qubits) in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s, "
              f"{len(gains)} improved, {s.obj} -> {new_obj}", flush=True)
        log.append(dict(round=r, programs=len(windows), max_qubits=qubits, improved=len(gains),
                        obj=new_obj, seconds=round(time.time() - t0)))
        s = qc.State(p, v_new)
    circuits = sum(sv.circuits for sv in solvers)
    maxq = max(sv.max_qubits for sv in solvers)
    used = None
    if svc is not None:
        time.sleep(5)
        used = credits0 - float(svc.get_credit_balance()["balance"])
    print(f"final {s.obj} (start {start}); {circuits} circuits, largest program {maxq} qubits, credits used {used}")
    if s.obj < start:
        settings = (f"start={a.start} kround={a.kround} rounds={a.rounds} layers={a.layers} shots={a.shots} "
                    f"cloud={not a.local} circuits={circuits} max_qubits={maxq} credits={used}")
        path, obj = qlns.save(p, s.v, "qlns-qaoa-cloudbatch", settings, log)
        with open(path.with_suffix(".log.json"), "w") as fh:
            json.dump(dict(settings=settings, start=start, final=s.obj, rounds=log), fh)
        print("saved", path, obj)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Batched quantum LNS on Qoro's cloud: large rounding windows, one per day, run in parallel.

Days interact only with their neighbours (rebalancing), so rounding windows on days of the
same parity (0, 2, 4, ... or 1, 3, 5, ...) are independent: their exact energy changes add
up.  Each round builds one window per day of one parity, sends every QAOA program to the
Qoro cloud at once (threads; each program = 2 circuits at transferred angles), and applies
every improving window together.  Same QUBOs and QAOA family as qlns.py (Dicke + ring XY,
p layers, angles transferred from the local runs), only wider.

    python portfolio_quantum/cloud_batch.py --inst po_a400_t15_orig --lam 1e-3 --start best \
        --kround 24 --rounds 8
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

import qlns
import qaoa_solver as qs

qc, ps = qlns.qc, qlns.ps


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--inst", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--lam", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--start", default="best")
    ap.add_argument("--kround", type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--shots", type=int, default=4000)
    ap.add_argument("--noise", type=float, default=0.1)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--angles", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "angles" / "a050_l1e-3.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--local", action="store_true", help="Maestro simulator instead of the cloud (testing)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    p = ps.Problem(a.inst, a.lam)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(a.seed)
    if a.start == "best":
        v0 = qc.load_v(p, qc.best_known_file(p.stem))
    elif a.start == "empty":
        v0 = np.zeros((p.T, p.n), dtype=np.int64)
    else:
        v0 = qc.load_v(p, Path(a.start))
    s = qc.State(p, v0)
    start = s.obj
    svc = None
    if not a.local:
        from divi.backends import QoroService
        svc = QoroService()
        credits0 = float(svc.get_credit_balance()["balance"])
    # one solver per thread (programs keep their own state); angles read-only (no retraining)
    solvers = [qs.QAOASolver(layers=a.layers, shots=a.shots, cloud=not a.local, seed=a.seed + k,
                             retrain_every=10**9, angles_file=None) for k in range(p.T)]
    lib = json.loads(Path(a.angles).read_text())
    for sv in solvers:
        sv.library["xy"] = np.array(lib[f"xy_p{a.layers}"])
        if lib.get(f"x_p{a.layers}"):
            sv.library["x"] = np.array(lib[f"x_p{a.layers}"])
    print(f"{p.stem}: start {start}, {p.qubo_vars} QUBO variables, cloud={not a.local}", flush=True)
    log = []
    for r in range(a.rounds):
        parity = r % 2
        days = [t for t in range(p.T - 1) if t % 2 == parity]
        windows = []
        for t in days:
            w = qlns.round_window(s, t, rng, a.kround, noise=a.noise * rng.random())
            if w is not None:
                windows.append((t, w))
        t0 = time.time()

        def job(item):
            k, (t, (tmp, moves, hw)) = item
            if hw is None and len(moves) > 22:  # free-weight windows would add slack: keep them small
                moves = moves[:22]
            res = qlns.run_window(s, tmp, moves, solvers[k], True, hw=hw)
            return t, moves, res

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(windows)) as ex:
            results = list(ex.map(job, enumerate(windows)))
        v_new = s.v.copy()
        gains = []
        for t, moves, res in results:
            if res is None:
                continue
            v2, obj, ncand, e = res
            if obj < s.obj:  # this day's window alone improves the incumbent
                v_new[t] = v2[t]
                gains.append((t, obj - s.obj, len(moves)))
        new_obj = p.objective(v_new)
        expect = s.obj + sum(g for _, g, _ in gains)
        assert new_obj == expect, (new_obj, expect)  # independence of same-parity days
        qubits = max(len(m) for _, m, _ in results)
        print(f"round {r} parity {parity}: {len(windows)} programs (<= {qubits} qubits) in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s, "
              f"{len(gains)} improved, {s.obj} -> {new_obj}", flush=True)
        log.append(dict(round=r, programs=len(windows), max_qubits=qubits, improved=len(gains),
                        obj=new_obj, seconds=round(time.time() - t0)))
        s = qc.State(p, v_new)
    circuits = sum(sv.circuits for sv in solvers)
    maxq = max(sv.max_qubits for sv in solvers)
    used = None
    if svc is not None:
        time.sleep(5)
        used = credits0 - float(svc.get_credit_balance()["balance"])
    print(f"final {s.obj} (start {start}); {circuits} circuits, largest program {maxq} qubits, credits used {used}")
    if s.obj < start:
        settings = (f"start={a.start} kround={a.kround} rounds={a.rounds} layers={a.layers} shots={a.shots} "
                    f"cloud={not a.local} circuits={circuits} max_qubits={maxq} credits={used}")
        path, obj = qlns.save(p, s.v, "qlns-qaoa-cloudbatch", settings, log)
        with open(path.with_suffix(".log.json"), "w") as fh:
            json.dump(dict(settings=settings, start=start, final=s.obj, rounds=log), fh)
        print("saved", path, obj)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---
name: portfolio-quantum-qlns
description: "Portfolio QOBLIB 06 quantum method (22 nov 2026): portfolio_quantum/ relaxation-guided QLNS with Divi Dicke/XY QAOA; what works and what doesn't"
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-11-22 the user asked for a *quantum* (QUBO) method on the portfolio track that beats the repo's earlier classical results. Built `portfolio_quantum/` (qlns.py driver, qaoa_solver.py, qlns_core.py, dayrelax.py, cloud_batch.py, campaign.py, report.py).

What works:
- Move-selection QUBO (one qubit per unit move, energy = exact Δ of the official objective).
- "Round" windows: per-day continuous relaxation (coordinate descent, neighbours fixed) → one qubit per fractional slot (trunc vs next unit). The day budget saturates, so the QUBO runs at fixed Hamming weight: Dicke state + ring XY mixer, no penalty and no slack. Swap windows use the flip y = 1 − x on unit-freeing moves for the same reason.
- QAOA angles p=5 trained once with COBYLA, then transferred with energy-std normalisation: 2 circuits per window, about a 50% hit rate on the exact window optimum.
- From empty, a050_t10_s01 λ=1e-3 reached −139 634 against the classical −139 048. The exact-oracle ceiling is −140 770.

What doesn't:
- λ=1e-2: rounding the relaxation destroys the hedges, and even the exact oracle finds nothing.
- At a400 the capital rule binds. This needs the warm seed plus separate XY rings for the +/− groups (`round_seed`).

**Why:** the earlier classical tabu/ILS search was stuck at λ ≥ 5e-4. The relaxation finds the right support, and the integer rounding is the part QAOA does.

**How to apply:** limit parallel QAOA processes to 2, because each takes ~700 MB (see [[macchina-ram-limitata]]). Cloud runs cost ~0.01 credit per circuit but have ~3-4 min latency, so batch the windows by day parity. Related: [[portfolio-classico]].

input.content:
# Portfolio optimisation (QOBLIB 06) with a quantum large-neighbourhood search

This folder holds a quantum pipeline for notebook 01. Every improvement it accepts is a bitstring
sampled by a **Divi QAOA program** on a sub-QUBO of the official model. The classical side builds the
windows, scores each sample with the exact objective and keeps the improvements. It never runs a
classical optimiser on the QUBO: no local search, no repair, no simulated annealing.

<!-- RESULTS -->

## How it works

**Model.** We work with one integer per asset and day, v = long − short ∈ {−3..3}. Holding long and short
units of the same asset never helps. The objective then equals the referee's
`qoblib_tools.PortfolioModel.score`. The cost function is `portfolio_search.full_obj`, which its `selftest`
checks against the referee. Every saved `.sol` is re-scored by the referee.

**Sub-QUBO (move selection).** A window is a list of unit moves (day t, asset i, ±1), one qubit each.
The energy of the QUBO is *exactly* the change of the official objective (`qlns_core.build_qubo`,
tested on 6 000 random assignments, 0 mismatches). The terms are:

- risk couplings within a day;
- returns, short and buy-in or liquidation costs, and cash interest as linear terms;
- rebalancing between consecutive days, which is exactly quadratic for one move per slot. Two opposite
  moves on one slot cost exactly zero when both are on.

**Windows.**
1. *Relaxation-guided rounding* (most of the gains). The continuous relaxation of one day is convex. It is
   solved with exact coordinate descent and a budget multiplier, with the neighbouring days fixed
   (`dayrelax.py`). It gives fractional positions v\*. Each fractional slot (up to 16 locally, 26 on the
   cloud) gets one qubit, which chooses between trunc(v\*) and one more unit away from zero. The
   relaxation saturates the day budget, so a window must add exactly `room` units. The QUBO therefore
   lives in a fixed-Hamming-weight subspace. Random noise on the returns and randomly excluded assets
   diversify the windows.
2. *Budget-preserving swaps.* These are unit moves on 7 assets of one day, in both directions. Moves that
   free a unit are flipped, y = 1 − x, an exact affine change of variables (`qaoa_solver.flip_qubo`). A
   saturated budget then becomes a Hamming-weight constraint as well.

**Quantum solver (`qaoa_solver.py`, Divi 0.16.2).**
- *Constraint-preserving QAOA.* The circuit starts from a Dicke state |D^M_k⟩ (`DickeState`) and uses a
  ring XY mixer (`divi.hamiltonians.xy_mixer`). Every sample therefore meets the day budget exactly,
  with no penalty term and no slack qubit.
- *Capital rule on a400.* There the rule C − 15 ≤ net ≤ C binds. The circuit then starts from the
  relaxation's preferred rounding (`CustomPerQubitState`) and uses one XY ring per group of +1 and −1
  moves, which conserves both counts.
- *Angles.* We use p = 5 layers. The angles are trained once with COBYLA on a real window, after the
  Hamiltonian is normalised by the standard deviation of the window energy. They are re-trained every
  300 windows and otherwise **transferred**, so a window costs 2 circuits: one loss evaluation and the
  4 000-shot sampling.
- *Transfer vs linear ramp.* On 14-qubit windows the trained angles, transferred unchanged, put about
  8× the uniform probability on the exact window optimum and found it in 4 of 5 unseen windows. A
  linear-ramp schedule found it in 0 of 5.
- *Backends.* Windows run on the local Maestro simulator, or in parallel on Qoro's cloud
  (`cloud_batch.py`). Windows on days of the same parity are independent, so their energy changes add
  up exactly (asserted in the code).

This folder holds a quantum pipeline for notebook 01. Every improvement it accepts is a bitstring
sampled by a **Divi QAOA program** on a sub-QUBO of the official model. The classical side builds the
windows, scores each sample with the exact objective and keeps the improvements. It never runs a
classical optimiser on the QUBO: no local search, no repair, no simulated annealing.

**Model.** We work with one integer per asset and day, v = long − short ∈ {−3..3}. Holding long and short
units of the same asset never helps. The objective then equals the referee's

checks against the referee. Every saved `.sol` is re-scored by the referee.

tested on 6 000 random assignments, 0 mismatches). The terms are:

- risk couplings within a day;
- returns, short and buy-in or liquidation costs, and cash interest as linear terms;
- rebalancing between consecutive days, which is exactly quadratic for one move per slot. Two opposite
  moves on one slot cost exactly zero when both are on.

**Windows.**
1. *Relaxation-guided rounding* (most of the gains). The continuous relaxation of one day is convex. It is
   solved with exact coordinate descent and a budget multiplier, with the neighbouring days fixed
   (`dayrelax.py`). It gives fractional positions v\*. Each fractional slot (up to 16 locally, 26 on the
   cloud) gets one qubit, which chooses between trunc(v\*) and one more unit away from zero. The
   relaxation saturates the day budget, so a window must add exactly `room` units. The QUBO therefore
   lives in a fixed-Hamming-weight subspace. Random noise on the returns and randomly excluded assets
   diversify the windows.

   free a unit are flipped, y = 1 − x, an exact affine change of variables (`qaoa_solver.flip_qubo`). A

class InitialState(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for initial quantum state preparation.

    Subclasses implement :meth:`build` to return a :class:`~qiskit.circuit.QuantumCircuit`
    of size ``len(wires)`` that prepares the desired state. Qubit ``i`` of
    the returned circuit corresponds positionally to ``wires[i]`` — the
    ``wires`` argument exists purely to let callers communicate domain-level
    labels (e.g. graph node names) that subclasses may need for length /
    shape validation.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def build(self, wires: Sequence) -> QuantumCircuit:
        """Return a state-preparation circuit on ``len(wires)`` qubits.

        Args:
            wires: Ordered sequence of wire labels (qubit ``i`` ↔ ``wires[i]``).
                May contain non-integer labels (e.g. graph node names);
                only the *length* and ordering matter for circuit emission.

        Returns:
            A :class:`~qiskit.circuit.QuantumCircuit` with ``len(wires)`` qubits.
        """

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable name of the initial state."""
        return self.__class__.__name__

    def product_masks(
        self, n_qubits: int
    ) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.bool_], npt.NDArray[np.bool_]] | None:
        """For a product of single-qubit ``Z`` and ``X`` eigenstates, which
        qubits are in a ``Z`` eigenstate and which in the ``-1`` eigenstate of
        their axis; ``None`` for any other state."""
        return None

    def compute_pauli_expectations(
        self, terms: PauliList, n_qubits: int
    ) -> npt.NDArray[np.floating]:
        """Expectation value of each Pauli string in ``terms`` in this state
        on ``n_qubits`` qubits.

        Simulates :meth:`build` with Maestro's matrix-product-state simulator,
        so wide registers work too; product states use a closed form instead.

        Args:
            terms: Pauli strings without phase, qubit ``i`` being column ``i``
                (e.g. ``SparsePauliOp.paulis``).
            n_qubits: Width of the register the state is prepared on.
        n_wires = len(wires)
        n = n_wires if self.n_qubits is None else self.n_qubits
        k = self.hamming_weight
        if n > n_wires:
            raise ValueError(f"n_qubits ({n}) exceeds the wire count ({n_wires}).")
        if k > n:
            raise ValueError(f"hamming_weight ({k}) exceeds n_qubits ({n}).")

        qc = QuantumCircuit(n_wires)
        for q in range(n - k, n):
            qc.x(q)
        if 0 < k < n:
            for m in range(n, k, -1):
                self._split_and_cyclic_shift(qc, m, k)
            for m in range(k, 1, -1):
                self._split_and_cyclic_shift(qc, m, m - 1)
        for q in range(n, n_wires):
            qc.h(q)
        return qc

    @staticmethod
    def _split_and_cyclic_shift(qc: QuantumCircuit, m: int, length: int) -> None:
        """SCS_{m,length} on qubits ``m-length-1 … m-1``."""
        theta = 2 * np.arccos(np.sqrt(1 / m))
        qc.cx(m - 2, m - 1)
        qc.cry(theta, m - 1, m - 2)
        qc.cx(m - 2, m - 1)
        for i in range(2, length + 1):
            a, b, t = m - i - 1, m - i, m - 1
            theta = 2 * np.arccos(np.sqrt(i / m))
            qc.cx(a, t)
            # Doubly-controlled RY on ``a`` (controls ``t``, ``b``) from CRY and CX.
            qc.cry(theta / 2, b, a)
            qc.cx(t, b)
            qc.cry(-theta / 2, b, a)
            qc.cx(t, b)
            qc.cry(theta / 2, t, a)
            qc.cx(a, t)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    block_size: int,
    n_blocks: int,
    wires: Sequence[int],
    connectivity: Literal["complete", "path", "ring"] = "complete",
) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:

content.text:
Ho un metodo quantistico basato su QUBO che **migliora i risultati classici esistenti su tutte e 5 le configurazioni su cui ha girato**, compresa l'istanza più grande della challenge. Nessuna però scende ancora sotto il best-known di QOBLIB: la più vicina è sopra di 18 punti (0,01%). Tutti i file sono stati ricalcolati con il referee ufficiale e risultano fattibili.

| Istanza | λ | Variabili | Qubit max | Quantum LNS | Best-known QOBLIB | Gap | Classico precedente | Miglioramento |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| a050_t10_s00 | 1e-3 | 3 110 | 18 | −191 256 | −191 879 | +0,32% | −190 685 | −571 |
| a050_t10_s01 | 1e-3 | 3 110 | 18 | −140 407 | −141 376 | +0,69% | −139 048 | −1 359 |
| a050_t15_s00 | 1e-3 | 4 665 | 18 | −312 668 | −314 736 | +0,66% | −312 312 | −356 |
| a050_t15_s01 | 5e-4 | 4 665 | 18 | −304 271 | −304 289 | +0,01% | −303 567 | −704 |
| **a400_t15_orig** | 1e-3 | **36 165** | **26 (cloud)** | **−3 015 526** | nessuno | — | −2 986 716 | **−28 810** |

**Metodo.** Ogni miglioramento accettato è un campione di una QAOA Divi su un sotto-QUBO esatto:
- **Sotto-QUBO.** Un qubit per mossa di un'unità. L'energia è esattamente la variazione dell'obiettivo ufficiale: su 6 000 prove non c'è nessuna discrepanza.
- **Finestre.** Un rilassamento continuo del singolo giorno indica quali posizioni arrotondare, e ogni posizione frazionaria diventa un qubit.
- **QAOA.** Parte da uno stato di Dicke e usa un mixer XY. Così il vincolo di budget vale per costruzione: non servono penalità né qubit di slack.
- **Angoli.** p=5, addestrati una volta con COBYLA e poi riusati: bastano 2 circuiti per finestra.
- **Parte classica.** Si limita a scegliere le finestre, valutare i campioni e accettare quelli che migliorano. Non c'è ricerca locale classica.
- **Qualità della QAOA.** Trova l'ottimo esatto della finestra nel **49%** dei casi (120 su 244 verifiche).

**Partenze.** Quattro dei cinque risultati partono dalla soluzione classica del repo e la migliorano. Il quinto (a050_t15_s01) parte dal migliore tra il classico e un run quantistico precedente sulla stessa configurazione, sempre a λ=5e-4. C'è anche un run **partito dal portafoglio vuoto**: su a050_t10_s01 arriva a −139 634, già meglio del classico, in 12 minuti. Con l'ottimo esatto al posto della QAOA lo stesso run arriva a −140 770, che è il tetto di queste finestre.

Su a400 il run sul cloud Qoro ha eseguito 7 programmi da 26 qubit in parallelo per 8 round, per un totale di 112 circuiti e 84,7 crediti.

**Cosa non ha funzionato o non è stato fatto:**
- **λ=1e-2:** il metodo non funziona. Arrotondando il rilassamento gli hedge si rompono e il rischio esplode; nemmeno l'ottimo esatto della finestra trova qualcosa. Lì restano i risultati classici.
- **a050_t10_orig e a050_t15_orig a λ=5e-4:** nessun miglioramento.
- **Rimasti in coda e non eseguiti, per tempo:** il confronto con il campionamento casuale (che serve a dimostrare il contributo della QAOA) e le altre configurazioni a λ=1e-3 e 5e-4.

Nota: un'altra sessione sta facendo girare 6 processi classici su a200, che rallentano la macchina. Non li ho toccati.

CLASSICAL PORTFOLIO RESULTS (QOBLIB 06, notebook 01_portfolio_optimisation.ipynb)
Reading guide for an AI assistant. Snapshot: 2026-11-22, about 01:20 CET.
All paths are relative to the repository root.

======================================================================
1. WHAT THIS FOLDER EXPLAINS
======================================================================

On 2026-11-21/22 we applied the classical recipe that worked on network24
(parallel tempering + iterated local search) to the portfolio problem, with
two problem-specific moves added: exact asset-trajectory DP and a day-level
tabu search. One campaign covered 125 (instance, budget, lambda) configurations.
No quantum program was used (0 qubits). Divi was not used.

Every .sol file in deliverables/portfolio/ passes the notebook's official
scorer, qoblib_tools.PortfolioModel.score (logs/verify_official_scorer.txt,
125 x OK). That scorer is the notebook's port of QOBLIB's checker. It
reproduces the published objectives of QOBLIB's reference solutions. We did
not run QOBLIB's own checker from the QOBLIB repository.

  group                         configs  below BKV  equal  above
  po_a010_* (8 inst x 7 lambda)  56       0          56     0
  po_a050_* (8 inst x 7 lambda)  56       6          34     16
  po_a200/a400 *_orig            13       no published BKV

  below the best-known value (BKV); lower is better:
  config                          ours        BKV        gap
  po_a050_t15_orig b020 l1e-2     -50,971     -31,504    -61.79%
  po_a050_t10_s00  b020 l1e-2     -19,785     -12,340    -60.33%
  po_a050_t10_orig b020 l1e-2     -44,208     -37,107    -19.14%  (*)
  po_a050_t10_s02  b020 l1e-2     -44,625     -43,565    -2.43%
  po_a050_t10_s00  b020 l5e-4     -234,696    -234,259   -0.19%
  po_a050_t15_s02  b020 l5e-4     -392,723    -392,668   -0.01%

  (*) PROVENANCE: this file comes from a run at 00:16 that was started from
  QOBLIB's published reference solution, with
  --init qoblib_data/06-portfolio/solutions/po_a050_t10_orig/po_a050_t10_orig_b020_l1e-2.bst.sol
  (see logs/log.csv, row 2026-11-22T00:16:10). It is a valid improvement of
  the published solution, but not an independent result. The run did not come
  from this session's job list: it wrote into the same solutions folder while
  this session was running. Independent runs from an empty portfolio reached
  -19,592 (hybrid without
  tabu, 2 min), -29,766 (tabu, 2 min) and -34,853 (hybrid, 3 min, seed 11,
  logs/development/a050_t10_orig_1e-2_independent_from_zero.log and .sol.txt),
  which is +6.07% above the BKV.
  The other five files below the BKV come from chains that started from
  the empty portfolio.

  above the BKV (weak spots):
  lambda 1e-2: a050_t10_s01 +55.5% (stuck at the empty portfolio, -1000),
               a050_t15_s01 +42.3%, a050_t15_s00 +18.4%, a050_t15_s02 +1.5%
  lambda 1e-3: all eight a050 instances, +0.28% to +2.76%
  lambda 5e-4: four a050 instances, +0.01% to +0.24%

HONEST SUMMARY (read before writing any claim):
- Short runs: 0.75 min (a010), 2 min (a050) and 3 min (a200/a400) per
  configuration with one seed. Longer runs would probably improve the "above"
  rows.
- QOBLIB's "best known" values for lambda = 1e-2 are weak (on a010 they are
  -1000 or -1500, the empty portfolio). The large negative gaps there say more
